## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)
**System Name:** Main House
**Maintenance Interval:** 12 months

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a CRITICAL pump problem that requires immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing only 22.2% of its nameplate amperage, indicating no hydraulic load. This is a confirmed failure mode. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is functioning normally, but the pump defect prevents proper system operation.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3.0 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8.0 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48.0 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The liquid level is at the outlet. The effluent filter is in good condition with light soiling and was cleaned and reseated during this visit.

## PUMP ASSESSMENT
| Component | Measurement | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Effluent Pump Amp Draw | 1.6A / 7.2A nameplate | CRITICAL - No Load |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Good |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | Good |

The pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load indicates the pump has no hydraulic load -- it is not moving fluid. The motor is at risk of overheating without fluid cooling. The most likely causes are a dry run condition (no fluid reaching the pump), a broken or missing impeller, or a severed or disconnected discharge line. The electrical connections are sound and the high water alarm is functional, so the fault is in the pump itself or its intake/discharge plumbing.

## DISPERSAL FIELD
The dispersal field surface is dry with no evidence of breakout or ponding.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. The pump is running without hydraulic load, which indicates impeller failure, a severed discharge line, or a blockage preventing fluid from reaching the pump. Do not continue operating the system in this condition. A qualified technician must inspect the pump, intake line and discharge line to identify and correct the fault.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is repaired and confirmed operational.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### Pump Failure
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious problem that will damage the motor if left unaddressed. The pump needs immediate inspection and repair. Until it is fixed, your system cannot treat and disperse wastewater properly.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at 22.9 percent of tank volume, which is within the normal range. Continue to keep non-biodegradable material out of the system -- wipes, paper towels, cooking grease, and medications all slow treatment and accelerate solids buildup.
